title: Thrashing
purpose: Illustrate CPU utilization rising with multiprogramming then collapsing under page swapping pressure.
requiredChecks: Horizontal axis is Degree of multiprogramming and vertical axis CPU utilization.
A qualitative curve first rises, peaks, then drops steeply under high multiprogramming.
Thrashing region is clearly labeled after the peak/drop, with an explanation of excessive paging.
No invented numeric measurements; caption marks the curve conceptual.
alt: Conceptual thrashing curve: CPU utilization drops when too many processes spend time paging
prompt: Create a NEW original English technical educational diagram. White background, crisp large navy sans-serif text, flat blue/teal shapes, minimal clean connectors, generous margins, no logos or watermark, no decorative or traced textbook artwork. TITLE "Thrashing". A qualitative line plot with navy axes and NO numeric data/ticks. Exact horizontal label "Degree of multiprogramming" and vertical label "CPU utilization". Draw one blue curve starting low at left, rising smoothly to a broad peak, then dropping STEEPLY toward the baseline on the right. Add a pale teal shaded band only over the right-hand drop region, labeled "Thrashing". Under the plot, note exactly "Too few frames → frequent page faults → excessive paging". Footer exactly "Conceptual curve, not measured data". Keep the label within the high-multiprogramming drop region, not on the ascending portion. Do not invent performance percentages or make the curve increase throughout.
